title: Book One · Chapter 16: Saturday Plans
story:
"Come early on Saturday," Ronan tells Leo.

Leo is trying to pack his book. His bag is full of a jumper. He pushes down with both hands.

"I can't."

"We need to make Jun's kite."

"My dad is taking me to my aunt's."

"After that."

"We stay for dinner."

Ronan pulls the jumper out of Leo's bag. Leo puts the book in and takes the jumper back.

"You didn't tell me."

"You didn't ask me."

Ronan stands still. At home, he told Dad, "Please ask me first." Now Leo is saying the same thing to him. Ronan does not like that.

"We have a job," he says.

"The other kite is your job. I agreed to make our kite."

Miss Wu asks them to clear their desk. Neither boy speaks while they do it. The stone goes into Leo's pocket. The drawing goes into Ronan's book.

At home, "Leo is going away," Ronan tells Mum. "I need his help!"

"For the whole week?" Mum asks.

"For Saturday."

"Does he know you'll miss him?"

"I need him to hold the sticks."

Mum looks at him over a shirt. She doesn't answer that part.

On Saturday morning, Ronan takes the kite things into the yard. The air is still. He puts two stones on the paper. He takes out a strip and starts measuring it against the first kite.

The black cat walks onto the board.

"No," Ronan says.

The cat sits on the paper.

"That's Jun's."

The cat closes one eye.

Mrs Lan comes out with a basket. She makes a soft sound, and the cat follows her toward the front room.

"Does it live with you?" Ronan asks.

"It eats at three doors. It may not have one home. Ask it!"

Ronan tries to tie the strips together. The long one moves while he pulls the string. The short one falls off the board. He tries again. This time he holds both with his knee.

The knot sits in the wrong place. He pulls the ends again. The knot stays tight.

Dad comes through the gate. He went to speak to a man about work. His face looks tired.

"Can you hold this?" Ronan asks.

Dad puts his bag down. "For a few minutes. Then I need lunch."

Dad holds the strips. Ronan loosens the knot. They put the strips back in the right places. Ronan ties them again. Dad lets go, and the cross stays together.

"Can we do all of it now?"

"After lunch."

Ronan wants to say it will only take a little while. He looks at the paper and paste. The kite still needs its whole tail. Dad cannot finish it in one minute.

He covers the paste pot. Dad goes to wash his hands. Ronan brings the bowls.

After lunch, Dad rests. Ronan folds paper for the second kite. He makes the two sides match without help. The strips can wait.

In the evening, Leo comes past the gate with his parents. He has a round bun wrapped in paper.

"For you," he says.

Ronan shows him the cut sheet. "I did this bit."

Leo nods. "Tomorrow afternoon?"

"After your lunch?"

"After yours, too."

Ronan takes the bun. It is still a little warm.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：loosens＝解松；match＝对应；Saturday＝星期六；wrapped＝包裹着的。

理解问题：

1. Leo 为什么不能按 Ronan 的想法来？
2. Ronan 最后怎样安排自己的星期六？
